scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The sole indexed destination combines St. Kitts and Nevis. Earlier partition dates apply specifically to St. Kitts; historical St. Kitts-Nevis-Anguilla institutions are not treated as the present two-island federation.

The archaeological report’s total reuse is budgeted as one work across all three object examples. No claim that Coconut Walk pottery dates every shell object independently is made. Jamestown material from several centuries is not treated as one sealed household.

The source gives chamber pots and basins around 1850 to 1880. Their precise household location and sewage arrangements were not established. Humour explains familiar terms rather than inventing a custom.
UNESCO’s erroneous broad claim that St. Kitts was the first West Indian island colonized by Europeans is not adopted. Its construction and labour descriptions are used.
The archives distinguish planned apprenticeship end dates from actual termination in 1838; this card follows the local Basseterre account for the latter.
The archives timeline and statehood article disagree by one day in February 1967. Only the year is given; no unsupported day is selected.
Christmas performances are described through the archives’ documented account, not as identical across every island, group or era. No current UNESCO inscription claim is made.
No imported geometry is changed or independently certified, and no unverified successor link is added.
